messages:
alex: Heads-up — gpool-us-east is showing a persistent backlog when streaming+sync mix hits. 95th latency spikes and a couple of GPUs OOMed. Logs above.
maria: saw open_streams peak at 420 earlier, limit is 300. lots of long chats holding connections open.
kevin: can you paste the evict/log lines? link to grafana?
alex: pasted snippet from node-23:
```
evicted_streams=31 blocked_sync_requests=602 gpu_mem_pressure=0.92 open_streams=413
"context": "user sessions with 40k token vistas"
```
sofia: hmm. is this more of a connection-slot exhaustion at the LB or genuine GPU resource exhaustion? both matter.
tim: infra-bot showed connection slots hitting 100% on the gpool LB 30m ago. :alarm_clock:
infra-bot: alert: gpool-us-east avg_conn_time increased 18% in last 1h; tcp_reuse low; conn_slots=1024/1024
maria: customers expect streaming low-latency; if we just deprioritize streaming we'll regress perceived quality. need smarter admission.
kevin: proposal: two changes — 1) token-weighted admission (estimate remaining tokens and weight), 2) dedicated tiny-stream pool for short sessions (<=512 tokens). smaller streams get streaming pool with fast path.
alex: dedicated pool looks promising but costy. rough reserve estimate: +6 p4d-months for steady-state in us-east => ~+$65k/mo. can we buy back with higher density (quantized models)?
sofia: alternate: implement preemptible streaming on shared pool: streaming requests are preemptible once gpu_util > 0.85; they get an early-fallback to sync/resume tokens. that avoids reserved GPUs.
kevin: fallback complexity: websocket streaming -> sync chunking or truncated results. we need client-visible retry semantics. add header X-Redwood-Fallback: reason.
maria: also worry about network H-O-L: long-lived streaming connections tie up HTTP/2 multiplexing. gateway should enforce max concurrent streams per connection.
tim: draft config suggestion:
```
admission:
  streaming:
    max_inflight_per_slot: 20
    preemptible: true
    eviction_threshold: 0.9
    max_connection_age_s: 300
  sync:
    max_inflight_per_slot: 40
    weight: 2
```
kevin: token-weight pseudo:
```
weight = max(1, ceil(estimated_remaining_tokens / 512))
if total_weighted_inflight + weight > capacity: enqueue or reject
```
sofia: let's also track metrics for any preempt/fallback: preempted_streams, fallback_rate, user_visible_retries, avg_resume_latency. We need these for canary decisions.
maria: per-customer opt-out: private deployments may object to forced fallback. add per-tenant policy flags.
alex: plan: run 10% staging canary with streaming_preempt=true + token-weight admission. if tail latency drops and error rate <0.5%, widen. I'll write the canary runbook.
tim: network note — earlier flaps we saw were from a noisy NIC on node-11. recommend bumping LB health checks and enabling conn draining before node OOM eviction.
kevin: implementation notes: gateway should tag streams with estimated_remaining_tokens at request start (from client or heuristic). runtime exposes an admission endpoint that accepts weight.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary job scheduled in cluster staging at 2026-03-19T02:00Z.
maria: tagging: please add grafana panels for weighted_inflight vs raw_inflight and preempted_streams.
alex: thanks team. i'll open a doc with the cost calc, canary steps, and per-tenant opt-out API. ping @ops oncall if canary shows >1% user errors. :+1:
kevin: +1. i'll prototype the weight calc and a small unit test for eviction ordering.
sofia: i'll write the client-facing fallback headers and docs.
maria: ack. schedule follow-up sync tomorrow.
alex: closing thread for now, will post the runbook link when ready. :rocket:
